/* ---- who draws the shell ------------------------------------------------

   The page around the route: the header row, the tab strip with its second
   level and the screen hint, and the modal. Same arrangement as the route
   drawer, one level up, and for the same reason - these are rebuilt as strings
   on every render, so a state change replaces the whole header and the tab
   strip whether or not anything in them moved.

   The app declares which pieces it draws, by name, and answers when asked to
   draw one. Declared, not guessed: a piece the app does not claim stays
   markup, and that is what lets this land one piece at a time - the header
   today, the modal when the modal is ready, and nothing broken in between, in
   the single file or in the browser.

   Every entry point the game already uses (renderTop, renderTabs, renderSubs,
   renderWhy, renderModal) keeps its name and its contract, because the action
   table calls several of them directly: `belltoggle` re-renders the header, and
   an action that re-rendered the wrong thing here would be a bell that does not
   open. Each one now asks first, and hands over if the app owns it. */

name: askNow — the decision on the table is written into the state
why: a modal is UI and is not saved, so a save written while a decision was open resumed into a quarter with no decision in it: measured in a browser, the bank letter with three options was on screen, the save beside it described that quarter, and after a reload the decision was simply gone
now:
/* ── the decision on the table, written down ────────────────────────────────
   A modal is UI: it is not in the save, and it never was. So a save written
   while a decision was open resumed into a quarter with no decision in it at
   all - the bank's letter, the offer, the choice, silently gone. `S.asking` is
   the fix: the state names the decision that is waiting, so a resume can put it
   back on the table.

   It is an id and a kind, not the event itself: events hold functions (their
   odds, their effects) and cannot be serialised. An event is looked up in the
   decks by id; a thread stage is *derived* from the thread record by
   renderThreadStage(), which is why a thread resumes at the stage it was on.

   It is cleared where a decision is answered - in resolveOption, and by the
   thread choice - so what survives is only ever an unanswered decision. */
function askNow(ask){ if(S) S.asking = ask || null; }

why: behind every home screen, the three soonest consequences as people coming to your door, nearer the sooner they land, carrying a letter or money, the news's colour above them (VISUAL.md, M6)

name: roadAheadSVG — the road ahead, as a strip of quarters

name: arrivalHTML — they arrive at your gate

name: boardLook — the boardroom, read from the register and the board

name: boardSceneSVG — the boardroom, drawn
why: a long window onto the city, the register framed on the wall with your share in gold, the board at the table with chairs as big as their stakes, hands up for the open resolution and arms folded against it, the chair's mark, and the bank's man by the window with a blue folder - red when a covenant is breached

name: cityLook — everything you own, where it stands

name: peopleLook — everyone in your life, read for a picture
why: the cast who are still here, warmest first, with their colours, age, money and whether a story is open; the dead to be remembered; your household (VISUAL.md, M9)

name: castFigure — a person of the cast, drawn
why: their own colours, grey past 58, agbada once they have money, a stick past 70, arms folded when they are cold, a gold mark when a story is open

name: peopleSceneSVG — everyone gathered in your compound
why: you in the middle with your household, the cast as close as they feel, the hostile at the edge, the dead on an easel; behind the People screen

name: storyVisitorLayer — whoever a story is open with, at your gate

name: bothLayers — two layers as one
